key_insight: In parents from Cameroon’s Buea Health District, HPV vaccine hesitancy was predicted nearly as well by simple logistic regression as by more complex machine learning models, with information gaps and low trust emerging as the strongest drivers.
clinical_relevance: A practical takeaway for vaccination programs is that improving vaccine information and institutional trust may matter more than focusing only on demographics when trying to reduce HPV vaccine hesitancy.
method: Cross-sectional survey of 1,156 parents of children aged 9–18 years.
Compared logistic regression, random forest, and XGBoost after feature screening with group LASSO.
Evaluated models on a held-out test set using AUC, calibration, and Brier score, with SHAP used for interpretation.
evidence_signal: On the test set, all models showed similar discrimination (AUC-ROC 0.841–0.870), with XGBoost highest at 0.870 and logistic regression close behind at 0.869.
watch_item: This is an internally validated single-district study, so performance and predictors may not generalize well to other regions or health systems without external validation.
paper_title: Predicting parental Human papillomavirus vaccine hesitancy: development and internal validation of machine learning models
